fixes.explanation: Yep. “Peter took Him aside and began to rebuke Him.” He says, “Far be it from You, Lord!” and “This shall never happen to You!” I think Peter's heart was in a big hurry, but the text just tells us what he said.
It really does say it, friend. “Peter took Him aside and began to rebuke Him.” Right after Jesus talks about suffering and being killed, Peter speaks up. He says, “This shall never happen to You!”
Not quite, baker. Jesus answers Peter with, “Blessed are you, Simon son of Jonah!” Simon son of Jonah is Peter. Jesus answers that big confession with a blessing.

An angel is a fair guess, friend, but Jesus doesn't name one here. He says this was not revealed to Peter by “…flesh and blood, but by My Father in heaven.” The answer Jesus gives is the Father. Angels show up all over the Bible, so I get the pick.

That's the word. Jesus says, “…you do not have in mind the things of God, but the things of men.” It's a direct line to Peter. It comes right after “Get behind Me, Satan!” so Jesus is plain with him here.

Priests do show up earlier, because Jesus says in verse 21 that He will suffer at the hands of the “…elders, chief priests, and scribes…” But in this sentence He says, “…the things of God, but the things of men.” Good memory, friend, just a different spot.

Right, and it sounds backwards. Jesus says, “For whoever wants to save his life will lose it…” Holding on tight ends up costing the thing you were gripping. Then He turns it around in the second half of the verse.
That's the opposite of what Jesus says, friend. He says, “…whoever wants to save his life will lose it…” So the one who tries to save it is the one who loses it. It's a surprising line.
